Jin was later made Attendant-in-Ordinary and kept near the throne.
Jin was later made Attendant Gentleman and kept near the throne.
侍郎 is Attendant Gentleman, not Attendant-in-Ordinary (常侍).
Wang Jingdu, Yifu's administrator of Dongjun, abandoned his city and fled. Chu Zhi and other senior officers all sent envoys to Jin to surrender.
Wang Jingdu, Yifu's administrator of Dongjun, abandoned his city and fled. Sima Chuzhi and other senior officers all sent envoys to Jin to surrender.
司馬楚之 is the personal name Sima Chuzhi, not a given name Chu Zhi.
Yifu's Administrator of Dongjun Wang Jingdu abandoned the city and fled; Chu Zhi the Administrator of Staff and others all sent envoys to Jin to surrender.
Yifu's Administrator of Dongjun Wang Jingdu abandoned the city and fled; Sima Chuzhi and others all sent envoys to Jin to surrender.
The literal rendering treats 司馬 in 司馬楚之 as the office Administrator of Staff rather than the surname Sima.
Yan's Ling, Yifu's administrator of Chenliu, surrendered the commandery.
Yan Ling, Yifu's administrator of Chenliu, surrendered the commandery.
嚴稜 is the personal name Yan Ling; Yan's Ling incorrectly splits the surname as a possessive.
He held Changding in stalemate and in repeated battles defeated Ding.
He held Helian Ding in stalemate and in repeated battles defeated Ding.
Literal English fuses 赫連定 into the nonexistent name Changding.
Supervising Secretary An Gu attacked Chang and took him prisoner.
Supervising Attendant Censor An Xie attacked Chang and took him prisoner.
安頡 is An Xie, not An Gu; 監軍侍御史 is a supervising attendant censor, not Supervising Secretary.
The full account is in An Gu's biography.
The full account is in An Xie's biography.
頡傳 is the biography of 安頡; Gu does not match 頡.
Jian died while serving as General of the Palace Attendants and Attendant of the Masters of Writing in the Secretariat.
Jian died while serving as General of the Center Army and Attendant Gentleman to the Minister of Education.
中堅將軍 is not Palace Attendants; 司徒從事中郎 belongs to the Minister of Education, not the Secretariat.
His son Shaozong, in the Wuding era, served as an aide in the Bureau of Fields of the Secretariat.
His son Shaozong, in the Wuding era, served as Adjutant of the Fields Section in an open office.
開府田曹參軍 is an open-office Fields-Section adjutant, not a Secretariat bureau aide.
He Guan, Taguan's younger brother, attended Taizu within the palace.
Taguan, He Guan's younger brother, attended Taizu within the palace.
Chinese 他觀弟和觀 names 和觀 (Taguan) as 他觀's younger brother and makes Taguan the subject who attended Taizu; the idiomatic English reverses the kinship and the career subject.
Taguan's younger brother He Guan, in Taizu's time, attended at the ruler's side within the palace.
He Guan's younger brother Taguan, in Taizu's time, attended at the ruler's side within the palace.
The literal English likewise inverts 他觀弟和觀, which is Taguan as younger brother of He Guan.
延興 is the Yanxing era; 'Yansing' is a misspelling that obscures the reign name.
He died in the Yansing era.
He died in the Yanxing era.
The same misspelling of 延興 as 'Yansing' appears in the literal line.
Shu Sun Jian was a man of Dai.
Shusun Jian was a man of Dai.
叔孫 is the compound surname Shusun; splitting it as 'Shu Sun' invents two name elements.
Biao said, "Wei Jian's failure carries its fixed penalty; a better governor will replace him. Your army should march west, or a small matter will overturn our friendship.
Biao said, "Wei Jian's crime of losing his post has its fixed penalty; a better governor will be sent again.
The idiomatic sentence imports the following unit's demand that the army march west; Chinese s0176 ends with sending a better governor.
Fearing his route would be cut while government troops held Henan, Yu ordered a northern raid; only when they withdrew did it end. The account is in the imperial annals.
Fearing his route would be cut while government troops held Henan, Yu ordered a northern raid; only when they withdrew did it end.
The closing cross-reference belongs to the next unit, not to this sentence.
Jian crossed the river; Xu's Yan fled to Pengcheng, and Jian marched east into Yan Province.
Jian crossed the river; Xu Yan, Liu Yu's Governor of Yan, fled to Pengcheng, and Jian marched east into Qing Province.
Xu's Yan fuses 徐琰, and 青州 is Qing Province, not Yan.
Jian crossed the river; Liu Yu's Governor of Yan Province Xu Yan fled to Pengcheng, and Jian then entered Yan Province in the east.
Jian crossed the river; Liu Yu's Governor of Yan Province Xu Yan fled to Pengcheng, and Jian then entered Qing Province in the east.
Chinese 建遂東入青州 names Qing Province, not Yan.
Zhu Lingxiu, Yifu's governor of Yan, abandoned Xuchang and fled to Hulu; Jian pursued, broke him, took more than five thousand heads, and reached Zou and Lu.
Zhu Lingxiu, Liu Yilong's governor of Yan, abandoned Xuchang and fled to Hulu; Jian pursued, broke him, took more than five thousand heads, and reached Zou and Lu.
Chinese 劉義隆 is Liu Yilong, not Liu Yifu.
Shizu made Jian Great General of Pingyuan Garrison and Prince of Danyang, with the additional titles Great General Who Conquers the South and commander of Ji, Qing, Xu, and Ji—Yifu feared his name.

Shizu, because Jian's martial renown shook the south and Yilong feared him, made him Great General of Pingyuan Garrison, enfeoffed him as Prince of Danyang, and additionally named Great General Who Conquers the South and Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Ji, Qing, Xu, and Ji provinces.
Chinese 義隆 is Liu Yilong, and the fear clause is Shizu's motive rather than a trailing dash.
Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde came to relieve Huatai; Jian and Daosheng met and fought them.
Yilong's generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde came to relieve Huatai; Jian and Daosheng, Duke of Ruyin, resisted and struck them.
Chinese 義隆將 names Liu Yilong's generals, not Yifu's, and includes 汝陰公.
Daoji's men starved and deserters fell away in chains, so An Gu and others could take Huatai.
Daoji's men starved and deserters fell away in chains, so An Jie and others could take Huatai.
安頡 is An Jie, not An Gu.
Daoji's army went hungry and deserters followed one another; thereby An Gu and others were able to lift the siege of Huatai.
Daoji's army went hungry and deserters followed one another; thereby An Jie and others were able to take Huatai.
拔滑臺 means they captured Huatai; 安頡 is An Jie.
He was posthumously titled Prince Xiang and buried by accompaniment at Jinling.
He was posthumously titled Prince Xiang and granted burial at Jinling.
The Chinese is 賜葬金陵, a granted burial, not 陪葬 accompaniment (that rite is stated later for Jun).
He was posted as Great General of Liang Province Garrison and additionally General Who Pacifies the West.
He was posted as Great General of Liang Province Garrison and additionally General Who Garrisons the West.
鎮西將軍 is the west-garrisoning generalship, not 平西 'Pacifies the West'.
He was sent out as Great General of Liang Province Garrison and additionally named General Who Pacifies the West.
He was sent out as Great General of Liang Province Garrison and additionally named General Who Garrisons the West.
Same office mistranslation of 鎮西將軍 in the literal line.
Jun gave his integrity to Taizong in hardship; sensing Zhu Ti's plot, he had the spirit of Jin Midi.
Jun gave his integrity to Taizong in hardship; sensing the Prince of Zhuti's plot, he had the spirit of Jin Midi.
朱提 is Yue's princely fief, not a personal name Zhu Ti.
Jun entrusted his integrity to Taizong and righteousness shone in hardship; detecting the change of Zhu Ti, he had the wind of Jin Midi.
Jun entrusted his integrity to Taizong and righteousness shone in hardship; detecting the Prince of Zhuti's treasonous move, he had the manner of Jin Midi.
Literal English likewise treats 朱提 as a personal name.
The note is a page citation, not a count of 3815 pages.
The note is a page citation, not a count of 2094 pages.
and the Southern Yan records all make Xing Murong Chao's administrator of Dongmou, with no mention of service under Song.
and the Southern Yan records all say Xing was Murong Chao's administrator of Dongmou, with no mention of service under Song.
The English fuses Xing and Murong Chao into one name.
candidateDispositions: Second English Yan is Yan Province, not Xu Yan
Liu Song as polity in the note
Following Biao is not a name; Biao is already surfaced
graph variant 勤, not a person
detector fused Xing with Murong Chao

unresolvedReferences.description: Meng Ming is a retrospective Qin exemplar; no independent activity date is in the packet.
Xu's unnamed brother is attested only as the father of Jian.
The year of Shusun Lin and Xi Mu's mutual denunciation and execution is not stated.
Xi Jin's Yao defeat is named without a reign year.
Zhang Senkai's own dates are not given in the collation notes.
